item.title: Quickstart
item.description:
Note

CircleCI Labs project, 0.x, not supported by CircleCI support. What is tested shows what CI checks, and Limitations lists what v0.1 does not do yet.

The orb is not published yet. Once it is, adopt Smarter Workflows with one setup job from the cci-labs/smarter-workflows orb (see orb examples or the README quickstart). Until then, copy the inline setup job from this repository’s .circleci/config.yml; it builds the planner from source and matches what the orb job does.

  1. Move your pipeline (jobs, workflows, orbs, executors) to .circleci/continue.yml. That file is the catalog the planner picks from. Nothing else in it changes.
  2. Add a setup config in .circleci/config.yml with setup: true, the orb, and one smarter/plan job (see below). Turn on setup workflows under Project Settings → Advanced, if they are not on.
  3. Start in shadow mode (mode: shadow). Use source: build with the go executor until releases exist; then use source: release (the default) so the job downloads a signed binary.
  4. Push to the default branch. The first full run traces every job and saves the impact map. On later pushes, open smarter-plan/plan.md in the plan job’s artifacts.
  5. Require the planned workflow’s check in branch protection (or smarter-gate if you use per-job statuses). smarter-gate is a no-op job and costs no credits.
  6. Switch to select mode (mode: select) when shadow reports look right.
version: 2.1
setup: true
orbs:
 smarter: cci-labs/smarter-workflows@1.0.0
workflows:
 plan:
 jobs:
 - smarter/plan:
 config: .circleci/continue.yml
 workflow: ci
 mode: shadow
 mandatory: security-scan
 policy-bundle: policies
 executor: smarter/go
 source: build
 resource_class: medium

Pipeline parameters

If the continuation config uses workflow when/unless on pipeline.parameters.*, pass a JSON file of the values the continuation will receive: set parameters on the smarter/plan job to that path (for example .circleci/pipeline-parameters.json). The planner uses them when selecting jobs and writes /tmp/smarter/plan/parameters.json for continue.

Pipeline parameters

If the continuation config uses workflow when/unless on pipeline.parameters.*, pass a JSON file of the values the continuation will receive: set parameters on the smarter/plan job to that path (for example .circleci/pipeline-parameters.json). The planner uses them when selecting jobs and writes /tmp/smarter/plan/parameters.json for continue.

Optional: guardrails

Copy policies/, edit the settings at the top of guardrails.rego, and pass policy-bundle: policies on the plan job (or --policy-bundle policies with an inline setup job). Every plan is then checked before it continues. On the Scale plan you can also push the same bundle as org policy:

  • limit it to the projects that opt in;
  • start with every rule in soft_rules;
  • leave the _test.rego file out of the pushed directory.

Run the tests with circleci policy test policies.

Several pipelines in one project

All pipelines of a project share its cache. Give each setup config its own map-key-prefix (default smarter-impact-v1) on the plan job. Restore keys match by prefix, so no prefix may start with another one followed by a dash: smarter-impact-v1 would restore the maps of smarter-impact-v1-demo. smarter-demo-impact-v1 is fine.

Requirements

  • Linux jobs (docker or machine with a known Linux image) for tracing. Other jobs always run unless you declare them with plan --trace-jobs (comma-separated name globs), for example self-hosted runner jobs. The plan report lists traced and untraced jobs.

Getting the most out of tracing

  • Put checkout in the job steps when you can. When it lives in a local command instead, the planner still inserts the reset right after that command runs.
  • Prefer GNU-friendly images (cimg/*, Ubuntu machine images). Busybox/Alpine tool images work too: the reset and collect scripts fall back to stat and busybox touch forms.
  • List runner or custom-executor jobs with --trace-jobs when the config does not pin a Linux image the planner can read.
  • Read trace_coverage in plan.json (or the table in plan.md) after a shadow run on main to see which jobs are untraced and why.
  • The default branch builds regularly. Maps live in the project cache, so they expire with its retention.
  • Approved images, if your org enforces them. Some orgs’ config policies allow only exact image tags, so an image pinned by digest can be rejected.

item.title: Demo monorepo
item.description:
A small polyglot monorepo that runs on Smarter Workflows. Every job does real but fast work, so you can watch the planner pick jobs from a change.

services/api Go, with a handler and a test
services/web Node, tested with node:test
services/worker Python, tested with unittest
libs/proto schema.json, read by the api and the web tests
docs/ Markdown, checked for titles and links
infra/ Terraform files, checked for their shape
scripts/ what the lint, docs, infra, security and e2e jobs run

The pipeline

.circleci/config.yml is the setup config. It builds the planner from this repository, plans .circleci/continue.yml (workflow demo) and continues the pipeline with the result.

Job Reads
lint the source of the three services and the schema, not docs
api-test the api and the schema
web-test the web service and the schema
web-bundle the web service (a job from the circleci/node orb)
worker-test a matrix over two Python versions, which always runs
docs-check docs/
infra-validate infra/
security-scan everything; it is mandatory, so it always runs
build, e2e the api; e2e attaches the binary that build persists
hold-deploy, deploy main only, after a person approves

On main every job runs, and its file reads become the impact map. On a branch only the jobs the change can reach run, plus smarter-gate.

The demo keeps its impact map under its own cache key prefix, smarter-demo-impact-v1, because the repository’s own pipeline shares the project cache. The scenarios in scripts/e2e/scenarios-demo.tsv check what runs for each kind of change, and Validation lists the results.
